decision_criteria.backtrack: Move backward when the subgoal uses an object, theorem, representation, limit, or premise before the workflow has constructed or certified it.
decision_criteria.persist_adapt: Continue by adaptation when the subgoal still names the same target object, preserves essential commitments, and the last obstruction taught a sharper mathematical premise, object, regime, or bridge to formulate.
decision_criteria.pivot: Change route family when the same certified obstruction repeats after adaptation and no new target-relevant mathematical information is being produced.
decision_criteria.quarantine: Hold the idea as visible evidence or analogy when it is illuminating but lacks target-object identity, transfer certification, source grounding, or essential-commitment preservation.
decision_criteria.stop: Stop spending active-loop budget when the subgoal has no meaningful target-object link or fails to generate new learning after repeated attempts.

policy.purpose: Control whether a formula, lemma, route subclaim, or proof obligation should be adapted, backtracked, pivoted, quarantined, or stopped during long-horizon exploration.
policy.title: Formal Subgoal Control Policy
universal_invariants: The subgoal must remain linked to the active target object or explicitly leave the proof queue.
Persistence is licensed by informative mathematical learning, not by fluency or difficulty alone.
A hard proof debt can remain active when it sharpens premises, definitions, or bridges.
Repeated identical blockers without new information force backtrack, pivot, quarantine, or stop.
Evidence-only, analogy-only, empirical, or transfer-risk routes remain outside proof authority until certified.
